messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — 503 spike seen on /v1/generate (hosted). 60s error rate 18%, 5xx count rising. Pager triggered to alex kim and maria gomez :rotating_light:

alex kim: seeing it. dashboards show 503s concentrated in eu-west-1 and small tail in us-west. latency trending up too. starting triage.

maria gomez: i'm mid-handoff — primary -> secondary just changed 5m ago. i'm still on calls, but alex you're primary now right?

alex kim: yep i'm primary. maria can stay as secondary. devon, can you pull deploys/rollbacks for runtime in the last hour? suspected runtime commit that landed an attention optimization change.

devon chen: on it. looking at git and deploy history. last runtime rollout batch at 18:12 UTC, commit 9f3b2c. No infra deploys in last 2 hours.

taylor reyes: support-oncall FYI - customer tickets coming in for 503s, some report partial responses then drops. sample customer id: cust-732. Please collect logs for impacted requests.

support-oncall: noted. I've flagged top 3 paying customers and increased monitoring. attaching request IDs in thread.

alex kim: initial hypothesis: runtime change + KV cache eviction pattern causing downstream 5xx from model containers. But need to rule out load balancer / infra. leo, can infra confirm node health and NLB metrics?

leo park: checking. infra telemetry shows healthy hosts but NLB 5xx count also rising — backend connection resets increased. Not many infra config changes. Could be a behavioral regression at runtime that surfaces as backend resets.

ops-bot: NOTE: Auto-scale policy triggered 2x on model-pool-2 in eu-west-1.

maria gomez: handoff note: i'm available for escalation if alex needs it, but I need to wrap the support call in ~15m. who is second-second?

alex kim: devon is secondary for runtime, leo for infra. security-oncall, can you confirm there are no suspected malicious spikes? we saw some odd user-agent churn earlier.

security-oncall: looking at rate-limits and WAF logs — there's an increase in malformed streaming sessions from a small IP range but nothing that looks like auth bypass. I'll keep monitoring. If it grows >5% of traffic, escalate.

devon chen: I pulled the runtime rollout: the 9f3b2c change modified attention window pruning; can reproduce locally a small number of 503s hitting the runtime's connection pool with high concurrent prefix lengths. Reverting is an option but needs canary -> full. Suggest rolling back in eu-west first.

alex kim: agree. mitigation plan: 1) rollback runtime rollout in eu-west-1 (canary) 2) temporarily increase connection pool limits for model containers 3) enable graceful-degradation routing: send new sessions to fallback smaller model-version (ramp) 4) notify customers of partial outage.

leo park: infra can do (2) and adjust NLB timeouts. I can apply pool limit change as config patch and do a rolling restart of model nodes — expecting ~3-5m per node.

maria gomez: adding runbook links: runbook/inference-503 (internal) and playbook/handoff-checklist. If anyone is unclear on rollback steps see the runtime rollback section.

alex kim: devon, can you initiate eu-west rollback and post the canary job link here? I'll coordinate traffic routing.

devon chen: starting canary rollback now. job: https://build.redwood/test/rollbacks/5421 (eu-west canary).

ops-bot: JOB UPDATE — rollback job 5421 started (owner: devon chen).

taylor reyes: Support note: outreach draft to affected customers ready, waiting for confirmation of mitigation before sending.

leo park: applied connection pool bump on model-pool-2 in eu-west. Rolling restarts queued. NLB timeout increased to 120s as temporary measure.

alex kim: good. monitoring — error rate down to 9% after rollback canary started. latency improving.

security-oncall: still no indicators of compromise. the malformed sessions look like flaky client libs. not blocking.

devon chen: canary rollback succeeded in eu-west. metrics: 503s in canary set are back to baseline. scheduling gradual rollback for remaining hosts in region.

maria gomez: quick handoff/coverage note for when i sign off: alex will remain primary until 22:00 UTC, devon is secondary for runtime, leo is infra pager, security-oncall stays on watch for 2h, support-oncall will handle customer comms. There's a 30m coverage gap between 02:00-02:30 UTC tomorrow where no dedicated secondary is scheduled; we should either patch a volunteer or route alerts to eng-sre.

alex kim: noted — i'll ping on-call scheduler to add overlap or route to eng-sre for that slot.

support-oncall: sent initial customer update to affected tenants: honest ETA and note about rollback. will follow up once region fully healthy.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — severity: high -> mitigated. 503 rate down to 1.2% across hosted, eu-west healthy. No data exfiltration detected.

maria gomez: thanks team. final runbook pointer: after-action note in #postmortems with incident id inc-2026-03-14-72. Alex, can you own the initial postmortem and include a short ops blurb about the handoff confusion and coverage gap?

alex kim: will do. I'll draft a blameless postmortem and include remediation: tighter rollout canary thresholds, mandatory 30m overlap on handoffs for primary/secondary, and clearer cross-team routing rules (runtime -> runtime oncall, infra -> infra, security triage only if anomalous signals).

leo park: also recommend an infra runbook step to temporarily raise connection pools automatically on rollout if latency > X.

devon chen: logging actions: I'll add a short check in the runtime deploy pipeline to abort if connection-resets > threshold during canary.

maria gomez: great. closing notes: if anyone is adding follow-ups, tag me. i'm stepping off in 10m. :wave:

alex kim: thanks everyone — oncall rotation updated and incident ticket created. good job. :thumbsup:
